title: The Role of Implicit and Explicit Demographic Signals in Large Language Model-based Student Assessment

bias_targets.methodology: Counterfactual prompting with explicit education levels and implicit conversational histories, measuring shifts in automated essay scores, feedback readability, sentiment, and response length.
Counterfactual prompting using explicit SES levels and occupational data to evaluate changes in LLM assessment scores and text accessibility metrics.
Evaluating variations in essay scoring, feedback readability, and response sentiment when prompts explicitly state a user's gender or implicitly signal it through conversational history.
Measuring differences in text accessibility and assessment semantic similarity when conditioning LLMs on specific nationalities (e.g., US vs. UK).
Assessing the impact of a user's primary language on the readability, length, and sentiment of LLM-generated educational feedback.
Testing the effect of explicit and implicit ethnicity cues on feedback length, sentiment, and automated scoring metrics.
Measuring variations in response readability and sentiment when LLMs are conditioned on a user's religious affiliation.
Analyzing differences in LLM-generated assessment metrics across various age groups using explicit and implicit demographic prompts.
